claim: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are trimeric proton-gated sodium channels.
source: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are trimeric proton-gated sodium channels.
evidence: This is a fundamental characterization of ASICs stated in the abstract, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: ASICs play a role in necroptosis following prolonged acidic exposure like occurs in stroke.
source: Recent work has shown that these channels play a role in necroptosis following prolonged acidic exposure like occurs in stroke.
evidence: This claim references 'recent work' indicating it is supported by prior research citations.

claim: The C-terminus of ASIC1a is thought to mediate necroptotic cell death through interaction with receptor interacting serine threonine kinase 1 (RIPK1).
source: The C-terminus of ASIC1a is thought to mediate necroptotic cell death through interaction with receptor interacting serine threonine kinase 1 (RIPK1).
evidence: This represents a hypothesis from prior literature about the mechanism of ASIC1a-mediated cell death.

claim: The interaction between ASIC1a C-terminus and RIPK1 is hypothesized to be inhibited at rest via an interaction between the C- and N-termini which blocks the RIPK1 binding site.
source: This interaction is hypothesized to be inhibited at rest via an interaction between the C- and N-termini which blocks the RIPK1 binding site.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior work that the current study aims to test.

claim: The study does not find evidence that the termini are close enough to be bound while the channel is at rest.
source: We do not find evidence that the termini are close enough to be bound while the channel is at rest and find that the termini may modestly move closer together during acidification.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the tmFRET experiments conducted in this study.

claim: The termini may modestly move closer together during acidification.
source: We do not find evidence that the termini are close enough to be bound while the channel is at rest and find that the termini may modestly move closer together during acidification.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the tmFRET experiments conducted in this study.

claim: At rest, the N-terminus adopts a conformation parallel to the membrane about 10 Å away.
source: At rest, the N-terminus adopts a conformation parallel to the membrane about 10 Å away.
evidence: This is a finding from the memFRET experiments measuring distance from the membrane.

claim: The distal end of the C-terminus may spend time close to the membrane at rest.
source: The distal end of the C-terminus may also spend time close to the membrane at rest.
evidence: This is a finding from the memFRET experiments.

claim: After acidification, the proximal portion of the N-terminus moves marginally closer to the membrane.
source: After acidification, the proximal portion of the N-terminus moves marginally closer to the membrane whereas the distal portion of the C-terminus swings away from the membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from the memFRET experiments comparing pH 8 and pH 6 conditions.

claim: After acidification, the distal portion of the C-terminus swings away from the membrane.
source: After acidification, the proximal portion of the N-terminus moves marginally closer to the membrane whereas the distal portion of the C-terminus swings away from the membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from the memFRET experiments comparing pH 8 and pH 6 conditions.

claim: A new hypothesis for RIPK1 binding during stroke is needed.
source: Together these data suggest that a new hypothesis for RIPK1 binding during stroke is needed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings that contradict the existing hypothesis.

claim: ASICs are members of the Deg/ENaC (Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel) superfamily.
source: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are members of the Deg/ENaC (Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel) superfamily, with relatives including the mechanosensitive MEC4 from C. elegans, Pickpocket from D. melanogaster and most recently identified, the heat-activated BRNTaC1 from S.s mutilans (Yao et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the protein family classification, supported by citation.

claim: ASICs have relatives including the mechanosensitive MEC4 from C. elegans.
source: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are members of the Deg/ENaC (Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel) superfamily, with relatives including the mechanosensitive MEC4 from C. elegans, Pickpocket from D. melanogaster and most recently identified, the heat-activated BRNTaC1 from S.s mutilans (Yao et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge about related proteins in the superfamily.

claim: ASICs have relatives including Pickpocket from D. melanogaster.
source: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are members of the Deg/ENaC (Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel) superfamily, with relatives including the mechanosensitive MEC4 from C. elegans, Pickpocket from D. melanogaster and most recently identified, the heat-activated BRNTaC1 from S.s mutilans (Yao et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge about related proteins in the superfamily.

claim: BRNTaC1 from S.s mutilans is a heat-activated relative of ASICs that was recently identified.
source: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are members of the Deg/ENaC (Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel) superfamily, with relatives including the mechanosensitive MEC4 from C. elegans, Pickpocket from D. melanogaster and most recently identified, the heat-activated BRNTaC1 from S.s mutilans (Yao et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yao et al., 2023.

claim: ASICs are located primarily in the central and peripheral nervous systems.
source: ASICs are trimeric, proton activated, sodium selective channels located primarily in the central and peripheral nervous systems.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the tissue distribution of ASICs.

claim: In mammals, there are four ASIC genes giving rise to six unique isoforms.
source: In mammals, there are four ASIC genes giving rise to six unique isoforms that can assemble into homo- and heteromeric channels.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ASIC gene and isoform diversity.

claim: ASIC isoforms can assemble into homo- and heteromeric channels.
source: In mammals, there are four ASIC genes giving rise to six unique isoforms that can assemble into homo- and heteromeric channels.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ASIC channel assembly.

claim: ASICs have been shown to be involved in pain sensing.
source: ASICs have been shown to be involved in diverse physiological and pathophysiological conditions including pain sensing (Bässler et al., 2001; Mazzuca et al., 2007; Sluka et al., 2009), mechanotransduction (Hermanstyne et al., 2008), fear conditioning (Coryell et al., 2008; Du et al., 2014), and memory and learning (Wemmie et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: ASICs have been shown to be involved in mechanotransduction.
source: ASICs have been shown to be involved in diverse physiological and pathophysiological conditions including pain sensing (Bässler et al., 2001; Mazzuca et al., 2007; Sluka et al., 2009), mechanotransduction (Hermanstyne et al., 2008), fear conditioning (Coryell et al., 2008; Du et al., 2014), and memory and learning (Wemmie et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hermanstyne et al., 2008.

claim: ASICs have been shown to be involved in fear conditioning.
source: ASICs have been shown to be involved in diverse physiological and pathophysiological conditions including pain sensing (Bässler et al., 2001; Mazzuca et al., 2007; Sluka et al., 2009), mechanotransduction (Hermanstyne et al., 2008), fear conditioning (Coryell et al., 2008; Du et al., 2014), and memory and learning (Wemmie et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Coryell et al., 2008 and Du et al., 2014.

claim: ASICs have been shown to be involved in memory and learning.
source: ASICs have been shown to be involved in diverse physiological and pathophysiological conditions including pain sensing (Bässler et al., 2001; Mazzuca et al., 2007; Sluka et al., 2009), mechanotransduction (Hermanstyne et al., 2008), fear conditioning (Coryell et al., 2008; Du et al., 2014), and memory and learning (Wemmie et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wemmie et al., 2002.

claim: The first structure of ASIC1 from chicken (cASIC1) was solved at 1.9 Å.
source: The first structure of a member of this family, ASIC1 from chicken (cASIC1), was solved at 1.9 Å and revealed the overall architecture of the channel (Jasti et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a historical fact about structural biology supported by citation.

claim: The structure of cASIC1 revealed the overall architecture of the channel.
source: The first structure of a member of this family, ASIC1 from chicken (cASIC1), was solved at 1.9 Å and revealed the overall architecture of the channel (Jasti et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jasti et al., 2007.

claim: A single subunit of cASIC1 is comprised of a large cysteine-rich extracellular domain, two transmembrane domains and short intracellular N- and C-termini.
source: A single subunit of cASIC1 is comprised of a large cysteine-rich extracellular domain, two transmembrane domains and short intracellular N- and C-termini.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: CryoEM structures of cASIC1 solubilized with styrene-maleic acid copolymer revealed that residues 19–41 reenter the membrane and form part of the lower permeation path.
source: More recent structures of cASIC1 from the same group using CryoEM on channels solubilized with styrene-maleic acid copolymer revealed that residues 19–41 reenter the membrane and form part of the lower permeation path: a feature that was termed the re-entrant loop (Yoder and Gouaux, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yoder and Gouaux, 2020.

claim: The re-entrant loop feature was termed for residues 19–41 that reenter the membrane.
source: More recent structures of cASIC1 from the same group using CryoEM on channels solubilized with styrene-maleic acid copolymer revealed that residues 19–41 reenter the membrane and form part of the lower permeation path: a feature that was termed the re-entrant loop (Yoder and Gouaux, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yoder and Gouaux, 2020.

claim: The C-terminus and the cytosolic portion of the N-terminus remain unresolved in ASIC structures.
source: Nonetheless, the C-terminus and the cytosolic portion of the N-terminus remain unresolved.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of existing structural data.

claim: The intracellular domains of ASICs are likely highly dynamic and largely unstructured.
source: It is likely these domains are highly dynamic and largely unstructured.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of resolved structure.

claim: The termini play a critical role in channel function and regulation.
source: Despite the lack of structure, the termini play a critical role in channel function and regulation.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the subsequent citations.

claim: ASICs have been shown to interact with stomatin.
source: ASICs have been shown to interact with a wide variety of intracellular proteins (Cullinan et al., 2021) like stomatin (Brand et al., 2012; Klipp et al., 2020; Price et al., 2004), NHERF (Deval et al., 2006), and CIPP (Anzai et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brand et al., 2012; Klipp et al., 2020; Price et al., 2004.

claim: ASICs have been shown to interact with NHERF.
source: ASICs have been shown to interact with a wide variety of intracellular proteins (Cullinan et al., 2021) like stomatin (Brand et al., 2012; Klipp et al., 2020; Price et al., 2004), NHERF (Deval et al., 2006), and CIPP (Anzai et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Deval et al., 2006.

claim: ASICs have been shown to interact with CIPP.
source: ASICs have been shown to interact with a wide variety of intracellular proteins (Cullinan et al., 2021) like stomatin (Brand et al., 2012; Klipp et al., 2020; Price et al., 2004), NHERF (Deval et al., 2006), and CIPP (Anzai et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Anzai et al., 2002.

claim: Intracellular proteins that interact with ASICs can influence trafficking, gating, and localization.
source: These proteins can influence trafficking, gating, and localization.
evidence: This is established knowledge about protein-protein interactions.

claim: Mutations and truncations in the termini have been shown to impact channel gating.
source: Moreover, mutations and truncations in the termini have been shown to impact channel gating as well (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2021.

claim: ASIC1a has a clearly demonstrated role in cell death resulting from ischemic stroke.
source: Of critical physiological importance, ASIC1a has a clearly demonstrated role in cell death resulting from ischemic stroke (Gao et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gao et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Inhibition of ASIC1a results in a dramatic reduction in neuronal death following ischemic event.
source: Inhibition of ASIC1a or genetic knockout each result in a dramatic reduction in neuronal death following ischemic event (Chassagnon et al., 2017; McCarthy et al., 2015; Pignataro et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chassagnon et al., 2017; McCarthy et al., 2015; Pignataro et al., 2007.

claim: Genetic knockout of ASIC1a results in a dramatic reduction in neuronal death following ischemic event.
source: Inhibition of ASIC1a or genetic knockout each result in a dramatic reduction in neuronal death following ischemic event (Chassagnon et al., 2017; McCarthy et al., 2015; Pignataro et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chassagnon et al., 2017; McCarthy et al., 2015; Pignataro et al., 2007.

claim: ASIC1a may lead to cell death by contributing to Ca2+ overload in neurons.
source: It has long been suggested that ASIC1a may lead to cell death by contributing to Ca2+ overload in neurons as this isoform has some permeability to Ca2+ (Xiong et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior literature supported by citation to Xiong et al., 2004.

claim: ASIC1a has some permeability to Ca2+.
source: It has long been suggested that ASIC1a may lead to cell death by contributing to Ca2+ overload in neurons as this isoform has some permeability to Ca2+ (Xiong et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xiong et al., 2004.

claim: A newer hypothesis suggests that ASIC1a can act as a receptor in addition to its function as an ion channel.
source: However, an intriguing newer hypothesis has suggested that ASIC1a can act as a receptor in addition to its function as an ion channel (Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior literature supported by citations to Wang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2015.

claim: During stroke, the pH of the extracellular solution falls, leading to a conformational change in ASIC1a which exposes a binding site on the C-terminus for RIPK1.
source: This hypothesis posits that, during stroke, the pH of the extracellular solution falls, leading to a conformational change in the channel which exposes a binding site on the C-terminus for serine/threonine receptor interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior literature.

claim: RIPK1 is a cytosolic protein with multiple domains including an N-terminal kinase domain, an intermediate domain, and a C-terminal death domain.
source: RIPK1 is a cytosolic protein with multiple domains including an N-terminal kinase domain, an intermediate domain, and a C-terminal death domain (Mifflin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about RIPK1 structure supported by citation to Mifflin et al., 2020.

claim: RIPK1 is known for its involvement in necroptosis or regulated necrotic cell death.
source: RIPK1 is known for its involvement in necroptosis or regulated necrotic cell death (Galluzzi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Galluzzi et al., 2017.

claim: RIPK1, RIPK3 and MLKL are necessary to form the necrosome which is the required functional unit for cell death.
source: Generally, RIPK1, RIPK3 and mixed-lineage kinase domain-like pseudokinase (MLKL) are necessary to form the necrosome which is the required functional unit for cell death (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about necroptosis supported by citation to Wang et al., 2014.

claim: L-ANAP has a small side chain, similar in size to a tryptophan.
source: L-ANAP, a derivative of prodan, has several advantages for measuring short intramolecular distances within an ion channel. First, L-ANAP has a small side chain, similar in size to a tryptophan (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a property of L-ANAP supported by the chemical structure shown in Figure 1A.

claim: L-ANAP is a derivative of prodan.
source: L-ANAP, a derivative of prodan, has several advantages for measuring short intramolecular distances within an ion channel.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the chemical origin of L-ANAP.

claim: L-ANAP has modest spectral overlap with the absorbance spectra of transition metals making it well suited as a donor for measuring FRET over shorter distances.
source: In addition, its modest spectral overlap with the absorbance spectra of transition metals makes it well suited as a donor for measuring FRET over shorter distances.
evidence: This is a property of L-ANAP relevant to the experimental design.

claim: L-ANAP has been used to measure conformational dynamics in multiple ion channels and other proteins.
source: L-ANAP has been used to measure conformational dynamics in multiple ion channels and other proteins (Gordon et al., 2018; Kalstrup and Blunck, 2013; Shandell et al., 2019; Suárez-Delgado et al., 2023; Zagotta et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The amber suppression method utilizes two plasmids for incorporating L-ANAP.
source: This approach utilizes two plasmids. The first encodes the channel with a TAG stop codon engineered at the desired site of labelling. The second plasmid, developed by Peter Schultz's lab and termed pANAP, encodes 4 copies of a tRNA as well as an evolved tRNA synthetase that together allows for the loading of a tRNA complementary to the TAG codon with L-ANAP (Chatterjee et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a description of the amber suppression method supported by citation to Chatterjee et al., 2013.

claim: pANAP encodes 4 copies of a tRNA as well as an evolved tRNA synthetase.
source: The second plasmid, developed by Peter Schultz's lab and termed pANAP, encodes 4 copies of a tRNA as well as an evolved tRNA synthetase that together allows for the loading of a tRNA complementary to the TAG codon with L-ANAP (Chatterjee et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a description of the pANAP plasmid supported by citation to Chatterjee et al., 2013.

claim: TAG codons in the N-terminus can lead to translation re-initiation at non-canonical start codons downstream of the TAG site in Shaker potassium channel.
source: Work on the Shaker potassium channel has shown that TAG codons in the N-terminus can lead to translation re-initiation at non-canonical start codons downstream of the TAG site (Kalstrup and Blunck, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kalstrup and Blunck, 2015.

claim: Conservative mutations were made in the first 90 base pairs (30 amino acids) of the channel to minimize the chance of alternate initiation.
source: To minimize this potential problem, we made a number of conservative mutations in the first 90 base pairs (30 amino acids) of the channel to minimize the chance of alternate initiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a methodological approach taken in this study, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The CTD has four native cysteine residues which were mutated to serine.
source: In addition, the CTD has four native cysteine residues present which were mutated to serine, allowing us to then reintroduce a single cysteine residue at a site of our choosing.
evidence: This is a methodological approach taken in this study.

claim: All cysteine residues in the extracellular region are engaged in disulfide bonds.
source: All cysteine residues in the extracellular region are engaged in disulfide bonds and are also too far away to contribute to a FRET signal given the working distance of tmFRET.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ASIC structure.

claim: Extracellular cysteine residues are too far away to contribute to a FRET signal given the working distance of tmFRET.
source: All cysteine residues in the extracellular region are engaged in disulfide bonds and are also too far away to contribute to a FRET signal given the working distance of tmFRET.
evidence: This is an inference based on the R0 values and structural knowledge.

claim: Robust mCitrine expression was only observed when both plasmids are transfected and L-ANAP is added to the media.
source: Robust mCitrine expression was only observed when both plasmids are transfected and L-ANAP is added to the media, indicating full-length channel expression.
evidence: This is a finding from the fluorescence imaging experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Omission of either L-ANAP from the media or pANAP from the transfection results in failure to produce full-length channels.
source: Omission of either L-ANAP from the media or pANAP from the transfection results in failure to produce full-length channels and an absence of any measurable mCitrine signal.
evidence: This is a finding from the fluorescence imaging experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Western blots were performed to ensure that full-length channels are only produced in the presence of the UAA.
source: To further ensure that full-length channels are only produced in the presence of the UAA, western blots were performed containing a number of potential TAG positions in the NTD, re-entrant loop, and CTD of the channel.
evidence: This is a methodological approach taken in this study.

claim: Position S485TAG shows no expression even in the presence of L-ANAP in the growth media.
source: Position S485TAG shows no expression even in the presence of L-ANAP in the growth media.
evidence: This is a finding from the western blot experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Position H515TAG shows channel expression in both the presence and absence of L-ANAP.
source: Position H515TAG shows channel expression in both the presence and absence of L-ANAP.
evidence: This is a finding from the western blot experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: S464TAG and M505TAG show robust ASIC1a expression only when L-ANAP is present in the media.
source: S464TAG and M505TAG, however, show robust ASIC1a expression only when L-ANAP is present in the media making these suitable positions to move forward with.
evidence: This is a finding from the western blot experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Each TAG mutant channel showed a robust current when L-ANAP was present in the media.
source: Each mutant channel showed a robust current when L-ANAP was present in the media (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the whole-cell patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Each mutant showed the typical rapid activation upon a fast switch from pH 8 to pH 5.5 followed by channel desensitization.
source: Each mutant showed the typical rapid activation upon a fast switch from pH 8 to pH 5.5 followed by channel desensitization.
evidence: This is a finding from the whole-cell patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: rASIC1a-G11TAG showed a slightly altered desensitization rate.
source: While rASIC1a-G11TAG showed a slightly altered desensitization rate, all mutants show complete desensitization in less than 10 s.
evidence: This is a finding from the whole-cell patch clamp experiments.

claim: All mutants show complete desensitization in less than 10 s.
source: While rASIC1a-G11TAG showed a slightly altered desensitization rate, all mutants show complete desensitization in less than 10 s.
evidence: This is a finding from the whole-cell patch clamp experiments.

claim: The pseudo wild-type construct, C469 WT, showed a half-activating pH of 6.52.
source: Our pseudo wild-type construct, C469 WT, showed a half-activating pH of 6.52 similar to our previously measured pH0.5 for WT ASIC1a (Klipp and Bankston, 2022).
evidence: This is a finding from the pH dependence experiments shown in Figure 2C, supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The pH0.5 values for the mutants all fell between 6.42 and 6.67.
source: The pH0.5 values for the mutants all fell between 6.42 and 6.67 indicating that normal pH-dependent gating remains largely intact in each mutant (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the pH dependence experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Normal pH-dependent gating remains largely intact in each mutant.
source: The pH0.5 values for the mutants all fell between 6.42 and 6.67 indicating that normal pH-dependent gating remains largely intact in each mutant (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the pH0.5 measurements.

claim: L-ANAP has been previously shown to not be pH sensitive when incorporated into the protein backbone.
source: L-ANAP has been previously shown to not be pH sensitive when incorporated into the protein backbone (Suárez-Delgado et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Suárez-Delgado et al., 2023.

claim: The emission spectrum of L-ANAP did not differ in either pH 8 or pH 6 buffers.
source: The emission spectrum of L-ANAP did not differ in either our rest (pH 8) or acidification (pH 6) buffers (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the spectrophotometry experiments shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The extinction coefficient of Cu2+-TETAC does not change when the pH of the solution is changed.
source: In addition, the extinction coefficient of Cu2+-TETAC and Co2+-NTA also do not change when the pH of the solution is changed (Figure 3C and D respectively).
evidence: This is a finding from the spectrophotometry experiments shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The extinction coefficient of Co2+-NTA does not change when the pH of the solution is changed.
source: In addition, the extinction coefficient of Cu2+-TETAC and Co2+-NTA also do not change when the pH of the solution is changed (Figure 3C and D respectively).
evidence: This is a finding from the spectrophotometry experiments shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The R0 for ACCuRET is 17.6 Å at pH 8 and 17.2 Å at pH 6.
source: This results in a minimal change in R0 values between pH 8 and pH 6 for ACCuRET (17.6 Å and 17.2 Å, respectively) and for memFRET (12.4 Å and 12.6 Å, respectively).
evidence: This is calculated from the spectral data using the Förster equation.

claim: The R0 for memFRET is 12.4 Å at pH 8 and 12.6 Å at pH 6.
source: This results in a minimal change in R0 values between pH 8 and pH 6 for ACCuRET (17.6 Å and 17.2 Å, respectively) and for memFRET (12.4 Å and 12.6 Å, respectively).
evidence: This is calculated from the spectral data using the Förster equation.

claim: Cell unroofing was used to gain access to the intracellular side of the channel.
source: Finally, in order to apply either of these metal labels to the CTD or the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane, we needed access to the intracellular side of the channel. To do this, we used cell unroofing which was originally used for EM (Heuser, 2000) but has been adopted for tmFRET experiments as well (Gordon et al., 2018; Gordon et al., 2016; Zagotta et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a methodological approach supported by citations.

claim: L-ANAP and mCitrine fluorescence colocalized well in the unroofed cells.
source: L-ANAP and mCitrine fluorescence colocalized well in the unroofed cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the fluorescence imaging experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: ACCuRET between L-ANAP at E8 and Cu2+-TETAC at C469 showed a modest 20% FRET efficiency putting the NTD and CTD ~22 Å apart.
source: ACCuRET between L-ANAP at E8 and Cu2+-TETAC at C469, the two residues immediately adjacent to the modelled close contact between the NTD and CTD, showed a modest 20% FRET efficiency putting the NTD and CTD ~22 Å apart which is significantly farther than the modelling predicted (Figure 6A, Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the ACCuRET experiments shown in Figure 6A and Table 2.

claim: The distance between E8 and C469 is significantly farther than the modelling predicted.
source: ACCuRET between L-ANAP at E8 and Cu2+-TETAC at C469, the two residues immediately adjacent to the modelled close contact between the NTD and CTD, showed a modest 20% FRET efficiency putting the NTD and CTD ~22 Å apart which is significantly farther than the modelling predicted (Figure 6A, Table 2).
evidence: This is an inference comparing the experimental data to prior modeling.

claim: ACCuRET for G11TAG and Q14TAG relative to C469 have similar results to the E8TAG position with modest FRET signals consistent with distances in the 20–22 Å range.
source: ACCuRET for two more positions along the NTD of ASIC1a (G11TAG and Q14TAG) relative to the same C469 have similar results to the E8TAG position. Modest FRET signals are measured again consistent with distances 20–22 Å range (Figure 6A, Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the ACCuRET experiments shown in Figure 6A and Table 2.

claim: Upon acidification, a slight increase in FRET efficiency is seen for E8TAG, G11TAG, and Q14TAG relative to C469.
source: Upon acidification, a slight increase in FRET efficiency is seen for all three positions, consistent with the NTD and CTD moving slightly closer together under these conditions.
evidence: This is a finding from the ACCuRET experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The NTD and CTD move slightly closer together during acidification.
source: Upon acidification, a slight increase in FRET efficiency is seen for all three positions, consistent with the NTD and CTD moving slightly closer together under these conditions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the increased FRET efficiency at pH 6.

claim: ACCuRET between G11TAG and Q14TAG and Cu2+-TETAC at C477 showed modest FRET efficiencies consistent with distances in the ~20 Å range.
source: In addition, we moved the site of TETAC incorporation out of the putative binding site to residue 477 and remeasured ACCuRET between G11TAG and Q14TAG at this new position. Again, we measured only modest FRET efficiencies consistent with distances in the ~20 Å range and a trend towards increased FRET at pH 6 (Figure 6B, Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the ACCuRET experiments shown in Figure 6B and Table 2.

claim: No FRET is measured between L-ANAP at E8TAG or G11TAG and Zn2+-TETAC at C469.
source: As expected, no FRET is measured between L-ANAP and E8TAG or G11TAG and Zn2+-TETAC at C469 (Figure 6A) indicating that the quenching we see in our experiments is due to the presence of the transition metal.
evidence: This is a finding from the control experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The quenching seen in the experiments is due to the presence of the transition metal.
source: As expected, no FRET is measured between L-ANAP and E8TAG or G11TAG and Zn2+-TETAC at C469 (Figure 6A) indicating that the quenching we see in our experiments is due to the presence of the transition metal.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Zn2+ control experiments.

claim: The lack of measured FRET in the Zn2+ control precludes the possibility that FRET between L-ANAP and mCitrine convolute the tmFRET measurements.
source: Additionally, the lack of measured FRET in our Zn2+ control precludes the possibility that FRET between L-ANAP and mCitrine convolute our tmFRET measurements.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Zn2+ control experiments.

claim: Cu2+-TETAC at C485 shows similar FRET at pH 8 to C469, but shows a larger movement (~6 Å) towards the NTD at pH 6.
